cover.caption: Myrsnipen er sikker på at barna hennes er de vakreste i hele skogen.
cover.alt: En liten myrsnipe står stolt på en mosetue mellom hvit myrull. Lenger bak går en snill jeger med stokk langs stien i skogkanten.

Create the cover illustration for a children's picture book, in a square format. Do not write a title or any other text on it.

Picture: Low, close view at the edge of the bog: the Dunlin, tiny and proud, stands on a mossy tussock among white cotton grass, her chest puffed out and her head held high, looking very sure of herself. Behind her, further along the Bog Path, the Hunter strolls through the sunny forest with his walking stick, smiling to himself. Warm midday light and two blue dragonflies.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Dunlin: A small, round-bodied dunlin in summer plumage, about the size of a starling, with a rusty-chestnut back speckled with black, a pale head and breast finely streaked with grey, a big black patch on her white belly, a long, slightly down-curved black beak, thin black legs and bright black eyes. When she spreads her wings, a white stripe shows along each one. A brave, proud little mother.
- the Hunter: A tall, lean, weather-tanned hunter of about thirty with a long, friendly face, a slightly crooked nose, crinkly grey-blue eyes, a clean-shaven chin and long, straight jet-black hair tied back with a leather thong. He wears a wide-brimmed dark-green hat with a long brown feather, a grey wool jacket with big patch pockets, brown leather knee breeches, red knitted socks and lace-up boots, with a leather game bag and a small brass hunting horn on cords across his chest, and carries only a crooked hazel walking stick.

Setting:
- the Bog Path: A narrow, winding footpath of trodden earth and pine roots running along the edge of a light forest of tall pines, spruces and silver-barked birches, where it meets a wide, open bog: soft green and rusty-red moss, tufts of white cotton grass, low heather, cloudberry leaves, grassy tussocks and small pools of dark water reflecting the sky, with low blue hills far away.

Story world: A forest in old Norway, long ago, where the birds can talk. A narrow footpath winds through a light forest of pine, spruce and birch and along the edge of a wide, open bog with white tufts of cotton grass, soft moss, heather, cloudberry plants and small dark pools. The dunlin's four chicks hide in a grassy tussock beside the path, a little way from where she first meets the hunter. The hunter is a kind man out for a stroll: he carries only his walking stick and a leather game bag. The dunlin and her chicks are natural birds.

This story's season, light and colours: A still July midday at the bog: warm sunshine with soft dappled shade under the pines, fluffy white tufts of cotton grass, ripening orange cloudberries, rusty-red and olive-green bog moss, dark pools reflecting a hazy pale sky, and a few blue dragonflies.

Art style: Warm Scandinavian children's picture-book illustration: gouache and watercolour on lightly textured cold-press paper, with soft coloured-pencil outlines and visible brush and paper texture. Rounded, friendly shapes and simple, expressive faces with clear emotions, but every character has their own face shape, nose, eyes, hair, build and age exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Base palette of moss green, spruce green, lingonberry red, birch white, fjord teal, honey yellow and warm earth browns, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours. The pictures are the colour plates of a classic printed storybook with warm cream pages, so the lightest tones are warm and creamy, never stark white, and lingonberry red is the accent that comes back in every picture. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Costumes and places from old rural Norway: spruce and birch forests, fjords and mountains, turf-roofed log houses, carved wood, rosemaling patterns, wool and linen clothes. Kings and princesses wear simple storybook finery. Trolls are huge, lumpy and mossy and look silly rather than scary. Clear, uncluttered composition with one focal point and room to breathe. Cosy, safe and full of wonder. Not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Gentle and safe for young children: no blood, wounds or gore, and no violence in progress. Show danger with mood, posture and distance, never with injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.

characters.name: Jegeren
characters.description: En snill jeger som finner noen rufsete fugleunger i gresset og vil ta dem med hjem, fordi han tror de ikke har noen mor.
characters.look: A tall, lean, weather-tanned hunter of about thirty with a long, friendly face, a slightly crooked nose, crinkly grey-blue eyes, a clean-shaven chin and long, straight jet-black hair tied back with a leather thong. He wears a wide-brimmed dark-green hat with a long brown feather, a grey wool jacket with big patch pockets, brown leather knee breeches, red knitted socks and lace-up boots, with a leather game bag and a small brass hunting horn on cords across his chest, and carries only a crooked hazel walking stick.

characters.name: Myrsnipen
characters.description: En liten fuglemor som ber jegeren la barna hennes være, for hun synes de er de vakreste i hele skogen.
characters.look: A small, round-bodied dunlin in summer plumage, about the size of a starling, with a rusty-chestnut back speckled with black, a pale head and breast finely streaked with grey, a big black patch on her white belly, a long, slightly down-curved black beak, thin black legs and bright black eyes. When she spreads her wings, a white stripe shows along each one. A brave, proud little mother.

characters.name: Myrsnipungene
characters.description: Små, rufsete fugleunger med dun som stritter til alle kanter, og som ikke sier annet enn «pip».
characters.look: Four tiny dunlin chicks, all alike, each a round ball of fluffy down no bigger than a plum. Their scruffy down sticks out in all directions: golden-brown and black mottled on top, sprinkled with tiny white dots like powder, and pale grey underneath. They have short, straight black beaks, shiny black bead eyes and long, thin grey-green legs with big feet, and they wobble when they walk.

illustrations.anchor: Midt på stien sto Myrsnipen og bredte ut vingene.
illustrations.caption: Midt på stien sto Myrsnipen og bredte ut vingene.
illustrations.alt: En liten myrsnipe står midt på stien med vingene bredt ut. Jegeren stopper midt i et skritt og bøyer seg overrasket fram.
illustrations.prompt: On the Bog Path, seen from low down at bird height: right in the middle of the path stands the Dunlin, tiny beside his boots, with both wings spread wide and her beak open, pleading. The Hunter, who was strolling along with his walking stick, stops mid-step with one boot still raised and bends forward in surprise, eyebrows high, one hand holding his hat. Pines and birches on one side, the open bog with cotton grass on the other. Bright midday sun.

illustrations.caption: «Stakkars dere», sier jegeren og løfter ungene forsiktig opp.
illustrations.alt: Jegeren sitter på kne i gresset og holder fire små, rufsete fugleunger i de store hendene sine. Ungene piper, og dunet stritter til alle kanter.
